paragraphs.source_en: Su Su was a passionately devoted girl. Like a wild rose, she wore her full, radiant beauty; Like a wild rose—her radiant beauty— a violent storm came and laid waste to her life. Here in the wild grassland is her grave; entwined in creeping vines, her grief is drowned; Her grief buried in the vines— ah, from this barren soil has sprung a rose stained with blood. That rose is the soul of the lovesick girl, nourished at daybreak by the clear morning dew, until evening, when the evening wind comes to warm and soothe her, and further still the long night gives comfort, with stars scattered like armies. You say that this is to be counted as her peace? But destiny again calls forth unfeeling hands to tear at her, to tear and tear away all the splendor on the green stems— How pitiful, Su Su suffers yet another ruin! Written in May, 1925.

淹沒在蔓草裏，她的傷悲──

那薔薇是癡心女的靈魂，

在清早上受清露的滋潤，

到黃昏

有晚風來溫存，

更有那長夜的慰安，看星斗縱橫。
